subgroups.name: solve 2

steps.hints: ❓Did you use quotation marks to separate the strings from the variables in showLongText ?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What symbols are used to contain strings?

❓ What symbol is used to join, or concatenate, strings and variables?


Solution:

Quotation marks should be added before and after each plus sign (+) so that strings are separated by variables in the showLongText code.
steps.instructions:
When the dialog box shows at the end of the countdown timer, it reads: “Wow! You stacked + cookieStack cookies!".


Fix the bugs in the code so that cookieStack is replaced by its value, when the dialog box appears.

subgroups.name: solve 3

steps.hints: ❓ What symbol should be used as an inequality operator in the else if condition to check if player’s guess is not equal to the cookie stack total?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ Which symbol should be changed so that the dialog box appears when the player’s guess is not equal to the cookie stack total?


Solution:

== should be changed to != in the else if condition under // on countdown end
steps.instructions:
When the countdown timer ends, a dialog box does not appear when the player’s guess is not equal to the cookie stack total.

 

Fix the bugs in the code so that if the player’s guess is not equal to the cookie stack total, a dialog box shows that tells the user how many cookies they guessed and what the actual total was.

subgroups.name: solve 4

steps.hints: ❓When the countdown timer ends, what Boolean value should be assigned to the canStack variable so that cookie sprites can’t be stacked?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ Which variable sets whether cookies can be stacked or not? 


Solution:

canStack = true should be changed to canStack = false under // on countdown end
steps.instructions:
After the dialog boxes appear at the end of the countdown timer, cookie sprites are still able to be stacked on the screen.

 

Fix the bugs in the code so that cookie sprites cannot be stacked, once the countdown timer ends.

attributes.description: You’ve reached Level 5 of Blue Belt! In this level, you’ll learn more about assignment and equality operators, which can be used to assign, change, and check for a variable’s value. Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 5:

badges.title: One Equals Sign or Two?
badges.description: Use the correct symbols to create assignment and equality operators to assign, change, and check for a variable’s value in JavaScript.

badges.title: Let There Be Variables
badges.description: Create a variable using let in JavaScript.

badges.title: Concatenation Station
badges.description: Concatenate two or more strings together using the + operator.

badges.title: Asset Depreciation
badges.description: Use the subtraction assignment operator to decrease the value of a number variable.

badges.title: Incremental Growth
badges.description: Use the addition assignment operator to increase the value of a number variable.

badges.title: I’m Thinking of a Number
badges.description: Use the askForNumber function to assign a user-inputted value to a variable.

badges.title: It’s Back on the Menu
badges.description: Write code that runs when the Menu button is pressed.
